articles.title: The Possibly Retired LEGO Super Mario World: Mario & Yoshi Drops to Its Lowest Price Ever for Prime Day
articles.summary: Nintendo fans have an opportunity to score one of the best LEGO x Nintendo collabs at an outstanding price, but you really don't want to hesitate. For Prime Day, Amazon is offering the LEGO Super Mario World: Mario & Yoshi 71438 for just $89.99 with free shipping after a 30% off instant discount.
body: The Mario & Yoshi set is impressively sized at nearly 16" tall and 5" wide with a relatively hefty 1,215 brick count. This is a mostly 2-dimensional build that looks amazing as a display piece on a shelf. Fortunately, it's not without its charming interactive elements, like a crank handle that makes Yoshi run with Mario on his back, and a dial that makes Yoshi's tongue pop in and out. Despite its simple design, this is a fairly challenging build that involves small bricks and technical pieces like rubber bands, hinges, and ball joints. LEGO recommends it for builders ages 18 and up. The end result is more than worth it, though. We built this set ourselves and absolutely loved it.

articles.title: A Scary-Looking New Conjuring Game Just Got Announced, And It’s Out Next Week On Netflix
articles.summary: Out of nowhere, Netflix and Until Dawn developer Supermassive Games announced a new The Conjuring game, and it's out next week. The Conjuring: Unspoken releases on October 13 through Netflix, so you don't need any dedicated hardware or controller to play it.
body: The game is an "interactive paranormal investigation" experience where players decide how the story progresses based on the dialogue options they choose. Players use their phone to walk through the fictional Red Lion Inn to search for clues about "things that go bump in the night," Netflix said.
You play as demonologist Francesca Noakes, and you'll use an electromagnetic field reader, an infrared camera, and spirit box to hunt for ghosts.
Netflix said you don't need to know anything about The Conjuring to enjoy Unspoken, but people familiar with the series will get "a lot more from the experience."
"There are a few familiar faces that pop up in the game, and knowing the backstory adds to the overall impact," Netflix said.

articles.title: Pick Up a 25-in-1 Hoto Precision Electric Screwdriver Set for Just $23 During the October Prime Day Sale
articles.summary: If you're constantly fiddling with small electronics, building PCs, or modding consoles and controllers, a precision electric screwdriver is an extremely handy tool to have around. For Prime Day, Amazon is offering an excellent deal on just that.
body: The Hoto screwdriver is a handy tool for situations where your large power drill might be way too powerful and a manual screwdriver would be too tedious. It's perfect for those tiny screws that require specialized miniature bits. This kit includes a total of 25 precision neatly stored in a magnetic clamshell case. The bits include pretty much every type you'll need, including Phillips, flat, hex, torx, U-shaped, Y-shaped, W-sharped, Tri-wing, triangular, square, pentagon, and more. Furthermore, they're magnetized so you won't accidentally lose those micro screws in tiny nooks and crannies.

The screwdriver itself is very compact, measuring about 6.2" long and weighing in at only 2oz. It is powered by a 350mAh lithium battery that can last up to 2 hours on a single charge and conveniently recharges over USB Type-C. It delivers up to 0.2Nm of torque in electric mode. That's enough to drive small screws without fear of stripping them. You'll want to use manual force to tighten the screws in the very end (or in the beginning, if you're unscrewing).
points: If you're constantly fiddling with small electronics, building PCs, or modding consoles and controllers, a precision electric screwdriver is an extremely handy tool to have around.

articles.title: Xbox Was At An “All Time Low,” But Is Now Growing Again CEO Says Without Providing Any Real Evidence
articles.summary: During a town hall meeting today, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma spoke to staff to help reassure them following mass layoffs and studio closures related to the "reset" of the business.
body: Windows Central reports that Sharma told staff that Xbox is "making the right decisions" and that "after an all time low, we've started to return to growth," though she did not share any specifics. She added that Gears of War: E-Day, Minecraft Dungeons 2, and World of Warcraft: Forever had "strong" starts, though she did not share any specifics.
Sharma said, "We've started to return to growth, more than 2 to 3 times what we were, and we expect that continue." She did not share any specifics about what "2 to 3 times" actually means, though.
Sharma also told staff that Xbox's "Gen-10" platform--AKA Project Helix--will be, as rumored, a "family of devices" because "there is no one device that fits all."

She said it's important for Xbox to have a "great console first," but there will also be options for players who are "on the go." Sharma went on to say that Microsoft will manufacture some of these devices, and others Microsoft will find partners for.

articles.title: Razer’s Wolverine V4 Controller Is Overkill For Most Gamers, And That’s The Point
articles.summary: Razer has officially revealed the next entry in its line of high-end gaming controllers, the Wolverine V4 for Xbox and PC. Geared toward competitive gamers--not that there's anything stopping you from using it to play Vampire Survivors--and it focuses primarily on polling performance and thumbstick…
body: One of the biggest changes is Razer choosing capacitive contactless sensors backed by a 16-bit analog-to-digital converter (ADC) for the thumbsticks, rather than the usual Hall Effect magnetic sensor. While Hall Effect thumbsticks are popular for their durability and for essentially eliminating stick drift, they can be prone to magnetic interference. Not a dealbreaker if you're playing at home, but in a competitive scene where victory is measured in fractions of a second, this can be an issue. In comparison, Razer is aiming to offer the same drift resistance, finer granularity, and smoother signal tracking with capacitive sensing.

Then there's the polling rate, which is absurdly high. For example, a DualSense Edge is capable of offering up to 1,000Hz (1 ms to 8 ms input latency), but the Wolverine V4 pushes that number up to 8,000Hz in both its wired and wireless configurations when used on PC, which, in theory, should put that on par with high-end esports mice and keyboards. This isn't the first Razer controller to feature an 8,000Hz polling rate, as the Wolverine V3 Pro was also equipped to reach those numbers.
points: Razer has officially revealed the next entry in its line of high-end gaming controllers, the Wolverine V4 for Xbox and PC.

articles.title: 5 Sci-Fi Series To Watch If You Love Lanterns
articles.summary: Lanterns recently came to an end, and it more than delivered when it comes to being both a great comic book series and a great piece of television. Not only did the series thrive thanks to the dynamic between Hal Jordan (Kyle Chandler) and John Stewart (Aaron Pierre), but it also managed to…
body: Now that Lanterns has ended, the question lingers: "What's next?" While Pierre is slated to return as John Stewart in Man of Tomorrow next year, some fans might want to watch a series to fill that post- Lanterns void on Sundays. Those fans are in luck, as there are plenty of series that manage to feature sci-fi tropes and elements alongside a compelling mystery or two. Here are five that make for the perfect binge-watch.

Much like Lanterns, Watchmen was met with mixed reception when it was first announced. Alan Moore's displeasure with adaptations of his work was well known at this point, and most fans asked why they should tune in when there was already a movie adaptation. However, Watchmen won over critics thanks to the way that it built on the original comic's events, while also weaving real history into its storytelling. It also weaves sci-fi elements into its narrative thanks to the presence of Doctor Manhattan, while still staying grounded. Fans looking for something that's similar to Lanterns definitely need to give Watchmen a look.

articles.title: Call Of Duty’s Richtofen Actor Wants Him To Come Back, Says 2027’s CoD Could Be From Sledgehammer
articles.summary: Veteran video game actor Nolan North has addressed his future in the Call of Duty series, saying he hopes to reprise his character Dr. Edward Richtofen from Black Ops' popular Zombies mode. If this does happen, it probably won't be soon.
body: Speaking at Gamergy in Puerto Rico ( via DomTheBomb ), North said he hopes Richtofen's story continues in a future Black Ops game, whenever that might be.

"I always like when they leave things open for the next one. I know that Infinity Ward and I think Sledgehammer has the next two before there is another Black Ops. I just don't want it to be the end of Richtofen, and I don't think it is," he said.

North clarified that he does not know for sure that Richotfen's story will continue, so he hoped people wouldn't think he had some inside knowledge apart from his own hope and belief. Whatever the case, North said Richotofen is one of his favorite characters to voice, and he hopes to reprise him someday.

North first appeared as Richtofen in 2008's World at War, and has reprised the role many times over in subsequent games from developer Treyarch. He's a fan-favorite character in the fan-favorite Zombies mode, with the story taking numerous twists and turns over the years.

articles.title: The 12 Best Video Game Series of the 1980s and '90s, Ranked
articles.summary: When we look back on the 20th century and the many great experiences it gave us, we tend to think of a few favorite video games that meant the most to us. But the medium introduced more than just our personal favorites.
body: A weekly cheat sheet to what you’ll eventually love to play. No buying, no commitment — just saving for later.

Can your refrigerator or toaster play Doom? The answer might surprise you. For decades, any devices with a modicum of computing power and a screen of some sort (and even a few things that lack such features) have been used to play Doom, the classic first-person shooter from id Software. The original game gave us a reason to hold LAN parties, introduced us to the depths of hell, and spawned a beloved franchise that in turn has inspired many imitators. Today, the series has fallen out of favor, even factoring in the success of the 2016 reboot and its sequels. But we’ll never forget the juggernaut it once was.

articles.title: 12 Biggest GTA 6 Questions the Previews Haven't Answered Yet
articles.summary: Since Netflix's extended look at Grand Theft Auto 6 debuted back in August, we've heard fairly little from Rockstar Games about 2026's most anticipated video game. That all changed on Sept. 29, when Game Informer shared its 14-page deep dive into GTA 6.
body: While there is surely more information to come in weeks heading up to the Nov. 19 launch, there are plenty of big questions about GTA 6 that we still have no concrete answers for. Here are a few that stand out.

Cheat codes are a foundational element of the Grand Theft Auto series, as much as flashy cars and the Wanted level. However, in all the preview interviews and footage we've seen so far, Rockstar has yet to officially confirm that cheat codes will return in GTA 6.

There's good reason to suspect that they will return, though. Both GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2 included dozens of cheat codes, allowing you immediate access to stylish outfits, infinite ammo, and top-tier vehicles (or horses). Enabling cheats in both games turned off achievements, but Red Dead 2 was a bit more strict in how it implemented cheats, essentially preventing them from being used to progress the main story campaign. Many of the best cheats needed to be unlocked by progressing Arthur's story and purchasing newspapers, and you could save your game while a cheat was active.
points: Since Netflix's extended look at Grand Theft Auto 6 debuted back in August, we've heard fairly little from Rockstar Games about 2026's most anticipated video game.

articles.title: My most-played album of 2026? Sorry, Mitski—it's Final Fantasy 10: House Grooves, a real thing that exists
articles.summary: Final Fantasy music is presumably so profitable for Square Enix that there are always new ways to slice the pie, whether we're talking piano covers, guitar versions, or expensive anniversary vinyl releases of its classic RPG soundtracks.
body: Elsewhere, Square Enix continues to find more inventive ways to squeeze dollars out of its vast music catalogue, including some which push the music into different genres entirely. Final Fantasy 10: House Grooves —the second of its kind following a similar outing for FF9—is exactly what it sounds like. Can Final Fantasy 10's often mournful or moody score become dance music?
The answer is: kind of. You never quite shake the sense that an unholy Seymour-Guado-and- his-mother -style union has taken place with this album.

Some of the remixes sound like music I'd expect to hear in the bar of the W hotel during GDC circa 2014. I'd say that definitely applies to the rendition of ' To Zanarkand ', the famous piano opening to the game. I get big 'making small talk with the concierge' energy from that one. Still, I do think the two styles ultimately gel in that case, even if the end result evokes vastly different feelings as piece of music.

' Phantoms ', a track players may remember from the icy Macalania sections of the game, is my favourite remix on there. I'd already heard this atmospheric track sampled in vapourwave and chillwave playlists from the mid-'10s, so the fit made sense there.
points: Final Fantasy music is presumably so profitable for Square Enix that there are always new ways to slice the pie, whether we're talking piano covers, guitar versions, or expensive anniversary vinyl…

articles.title: Someone's modded Diablo 2 for VR, and seeing the world through your character's eyes brings a whole new dimension to the series
articles.summary: Of all the games I thought I'd see converted to virtual reality, the Diablo games weren't among them, for some reason. But one industrious modder has set about changing that, converting probably the most well-liked Diablo game, Diablo 2.
body: Footage of the Diablo 2 VR mod was shared on Reddit and it shows the game being played in first-person, as the Sorceress explores the dingy starting area fields of the game, fireballing zombies and other enemies that are shambling nearby. It seems to work pretty well, with the player's left forearm showing the character's health and mana pools, and toolbar, and the inventory on their belt and map in their hand.

The Diablo 2 VR mod is made by Sergious - Reddit username Fantastic-Author2736 - and the mod files are made available on Github, should you wish to try it. Sergious made the mod with FlatVR and BodyWalk, but you don't need BodyWalk, apparently, to play it.

It's strikingly atmospheric seeing Diablo's world this way, through the character's eyes. The world is usually so far below you, as you look over it like a god from above, from an isometric vantage point. Not for the first time, it's made me wonder what Diablo would be like played from a much closer, over-the-shoulder camera angle, or even a first-person one. I'd half-expected Diablo 5 - recently announced at BlizzCon - to go this way, though it doesn't appear to be.
points: Of all the games I thought I'd see converted to virtual reality, the Diablo games weren't among them, for some reason.
But one industrious modder has set about changing that, converting probably the most well-liked Diablo game, Diablo 2.

articles.title: "Keep it family friendly" - Sega's official Sonic Discord swarmed by 50,000 people in six hours, as understandably strict moderation is put in place
articles.summary: Sega has invited chaos upon itself by launching an official Sonic the Hedgehog Discord channel. Unsurprisingly, it's proven immediately popular, and strictly locked down. There is no fan art channel as of writing.
body: The announcement, made on official Sega social media accounts, reads as follows: "Looking for a place to chill and chat all things Sonic the Hedgehog? Maybe find people to race in Sonic Racing: CrossWorlds? We are excited to welcome you to the official Sonic Discord server!"

This post, made on X late last night, invited hordes of Sonic fans into the hub all at once, where there are various channels for discussion of Sonic games, movies, and comics. There's even an off-topic channel, which seems potentially unwise, and when Eurogamer explored the Discord server today, strict moderation features were in place.

For example, the server is currently on slow mode, meaning the quantity of posts made in each channel has been drastically reduced. There are also chat limitations in place, preventing newcomers to the server from posting at all unless they use a Discord Nitro boost (a paid service). A plea to "keep it family friendly" is present on the rules page as well.
points: Sega has invited chaos upon itself by launching an official Sonic the Hedgehog Discord channel.
